- The executed credit agreement, its nine amendments and the three senior-note indentures are not supplied. The exhibit lists name them and the filings summarise them, but no operative text is available, so covenant definitions, baskets, call schedules, guarantor release terms and collateral cannot be read. Legal & covenants and Recovery & fulcrum are blocked, and Security selection is conditional on this text. Remedy: obtain the credit agreement through Amendment No. 9 and the indentures for the two 2029 senior notes and the 2034 senior notes. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 150–152; 10-Q_2026-06-30_apg-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 64–65 - No rating agency report is supplied. The only rating statement is in the 2025 lease note, which says the S&P rating of BB and the Moody's corporate family rating of Ba2 were stable in 2025. No issue-level rating, outlook or 2026 rating action is stated, so Ratings & triggers is conditional on an agency report. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 119 - No dated trade quotes, yields or spreads for the notes or the term loan are supplied, and the run settings list no quotes. The only market-based figures are the issuer's own fair value estimates by instrument, which discount cash flows at current rates and are not quotes. Market-implied risk and the pricing side of Security selection cannot be done until a dated quote set is provided. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 113 - No peer financials are supplied. The annual report names a share-return peer group only, and the run settings list no peers, so Peer benchmark is conditional on a peer set. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 58–59 - No portfolio or fund limits are supplied. Committee decision will state the fund's limits as not supplied. - Governance and ownership evidence is partial. The annual report incorporates director, compensation and ownership detail by reference to a proxy statement that is not supplied; officers and the 2026 officer changes are printed, and no controlling parent or sponsor is named in the supplied text. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21; 10-Q_2026-06-30_apg-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 64 - Perimeter is consolidated only. The borrower and note issuer is a wholly owned subsidiary, but the statements are consolidated for the listed registrant, and the supplied text gives no guarantor or non-guarantor summarised information and no list of guarantor subsidiaries. Debt, leverage and cash figures cannot be split by borrower group or guarantor group. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25 - The issuing entity of the senior notes is described two ways. The liquidity discussion says the wholly owned subsidiary APi Group DE, Inc. completed each offering and the 2034 indenture names it as issuer, while the debt note says the Company completed the 2029 offerings, and the 2025 exhibit index lists the June 2021 indenture as made by APi Group Corporation and the October 2021 indenture as made by APi Escrow Corp., with later supplemental indentures that involve the subsidiary. Both descriptions are kept; the borrower, issuer and guarantor perimeter must be confirmed from the indentures before leverage is read on a borrower-group basis. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 150; 10-Q_2026-06-30_apg-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 65 - The only maturity ladder is in the annual report and predates the May 2026 amendment and the 2034 notes. The latest quarterly report prints maturity dates but no ladder, and the term loan amortisation is described differently across the reports: the annual report says no quarterly principal is owed, while the latest report states annual instalments of 1.00% of the initial principal, and the initial principal is stated in two ways. Scheduled principal by year therefore cannot be stated from the supplied text. Financial foundation must build the ladder from the debt table and flag this. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 123; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 59 - Several 2025 year-end terms are superseded by the Ninth Amendment and must not be carried forward: the term loan maturity moved from 2029 to 2033, the revolver grew from USD 750 million to USD 1,000 million with maturity moving from 2030 to 2031, the covenant exclusion for undrawn letters of credit moved from USD 40 million to USD 60 million, and the first lien net leverage ratio moved from 1.1 times to 1.6 times. The newest report controls each term. These are period changes, not conflicts. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest contrary evidence is earnings momentum: nine-month adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 896 million from USD 746 million, nine-month operating cash flow rose, and the nearest large maturity is the 2029 notes. Adjusted leverage of 3.00x total and 2.69x net at 2026-09-30 is below reported leverage and would fall further if earnings from acquisitions closed during the year were annualised, but the filings do not state those earnings. A partial revolver repayment from operating cash flow, or disclosed pro forma earnings for the acquisitions, would move the view toward lower leverage; further debt-funded acquisitions or a larger working capital outflow would move it the other way. - Severity high. Covenant headroom cannot be measured: the credit agreement and its EBITDA definition are not supplied, the releases define a net leverage ratio but print no value, and only the first lien ratio is reported. The action is to obtain the credit agreement and compliance certificates. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_apg-20260930xexx991.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 60 - Severity high. The term loan's security and ranking, and the guarantor perimeter, are not stated in any supplied document, so the debt stack leaves out the largest facility and borrower-group leverage cannot be shown. The action is to obtain the credit agreement and the indentures. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 24–25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 58 - Severity medium. No maturity ladder is printed after the 2026 amendment and the 2034 notes, and the term loan amortization base is described two ways, so scheduled principal by year is not established and the ladder shown puts amortization at final maturity. The action is to obtain the amended credit agreement schedule. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 123; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 59 - Severity medium. EBITDA for FY2024 and FY2025 is calculated because the annual report states no EBITDA subtotal, and trailing EBITDA at each 2026 date carries acquired businesses only from their closing dates, so run-rate leverage is not established. The action is to obtain pro forma acquired EBITDA for the three large acquisitions. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 67–68; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9 - Severity medium. Cash interest is reported net of interest income and lags interest expense after the 2034 notes, so gross interest paid is not stated and interest cover on a cash basis is flattered. The action is to obtain gross interest paid and the 2034 coupon dates. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25 - Severity low. Carrying value by instrument is not disclosed, only the total of deferred financing costs, so each instrument is shown at principal with one financing cost adjustment. The action is to obtain the debt footnote detail. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23 - Severity low. Several statement lines are printed as dashes, for example investment expense in FY2025 and the first quarter of 2025, and no filing line is read as zero; each is stated as not supplied. The action is to treat a dash as nil only where a later filing confirms it. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 86; 10-Q_2026-03-31_apg-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 3 - Severity low. Balance sheets at 2025-03-31, 2025-06-30 and 2025-09-30 are not in the supplied documents, so prior-year interim net debt and leverage are not established. The action is to obtain the 2025 quarterly reports. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3 - Severity low. Remaining performance obligations are not stated for the 2024 year end or the 2025 quarter ends, and the backlog figure the second-quarter release cites is not defined, so the operating trend covers four dates. The action is to obtain the 2025 quarterly reports and the backlog definition. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 107; EX-99.1_2026-07-30_apg-20260630xexx991.htm.jsonl, page 1 - Severity medium. The effect of the borrowing of USD 100 million after quarter end on net debt is not established because the use of proceeds and the cash balance at 2026-10-29 are not stated. The action is to read the next quarterly report. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24 - Severity low. The Q2 and Q3 discrete income statement columns are not printed here; they are reported in the quarterly reports and the stub columns are used to build trailing figures. The action is to add discrete quarters if the forward model needs them. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_apg-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Ownership is not disclosed in the supplied documents beyond one equity-linked instrument that matters to creditors. The Series A preferred, held through a vehicle controlled by a board co-chair, entitles its holder to an annual dividend equal to 20% of the rise in the share price above its previous high-water mark, applied to a fixed block of shares, which was USD 590 million for 2025 and was settled in new shares in January 2026. The dividend is payable in shares or cash at the board's election and the company states it intends to use shares, so the mechanism is dilution today; a cash election would create a large claim that ranks ahead of common equity, and the 2026 dividend and conversion into common shares fall at the end of 2026. A related entity of a co-chair also receives advisory fees of USD 4 million a year, which is small but is cash paid to a shareholder-linked party. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that value going to shareholders has mostly been settled in shares or has been small: no cash dividend on common shares, a Series A dividend settled in shares, advisory fees of only USD 4 million a year, and USD 458 million of equity raised in 2024 to help fund the Elevated acquisition. The company has also used amendments to extend maturities and enlarge the revolver rather than to weaken creditor terms, as far as the supplied summaries show. A move to cash settlement of the Series A dividend, repurchases that exceed free cash flow for a sustained period, or a further large acquisition paid mainly in debt would move the view toward higher governance and financial-policy risk. Disclosure of ownership percentages, pro forma acquired earnings and the credit agreement's distribution limits would reduce the uncertainty in either direction. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence for a better view is that trailing figures include acquired businesses only from their closing dates, so leverage of 3.21x net may overstate the run-rate, and that earnings have grown 20.11% in nine months with no maturity pressure until 2029. If acquired earnings are disclosed and are material, or if the revolver is repaid from operating cash flow, leverage could fall toward the year-end level. The strongest evidence for a worse view is that interest cover on current expense is lower than on cash paid, that free cash flow conversion fell, and that the legal limits on further debt-funded buybacks and acquisitions are unknown. A further large debt-funded acquisition, a rise in revolver use, or a margin fall below the current 30.82% would move the view toward weaker credit quality. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-1; calculation CALC-2; calculation CALC-5; calculation CALC-9

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Credit strengths are the diversified, inspection-led service model, earnings momentum and a long-dated maturity profile. The service model spreads revenue across two segments, many customers and several countries, and inspection work is often required by law or insurance, which supports demand through a downturn; nine-month adjusted EBITDA growth of 20.11% shows that demand is converting into earnings. Debt matures late, with USD 614 million due in 2029, USD 335 million of revolver in 2031, USD 2,147 million of term loan in 2033 and USD 500 million of notes in 2034, so scheduled refinancing pressure is distant. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-5; calculation CALC-8

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Credit weaknesses are rising leverage, thinner liquidity and weaker cash conversion. Net leverage of 3.21x against 2.10x at the year end reflects acquisitions and buybacks funded by debt and cash; liquidity fell by USD 625 million; and free cash flow conversion fell as working capital grew. A related weakness is the lack of evidence on legal capacity and ownership, which leaves the limits on further distributions and borrowing unknown. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-1; calculation CALC-3; calculation CALC-6

facts.label: Downside pathway and outlook
facts.text: The realistic downside starts with slower contracting demand or higher tariff-driven material costs. Growth is concentrated in the lower-margin Specialty Services segment, which is 32.92% of revenue, grew 26.63% in nine months against 13.07% for Safety Services and earns a segment margin of 10.87% against 16.74%, so a slowdown there would be expected to hit earnings and working capital first. Lower volume and margin reduce earnings and leave working capital tied up, so free cash flow weakens while acquisition integration costs and buybacks continue; the revolver then funds the gap, undrawn liquidity falls below its current USD 1,032 million, and revolver use stays above the 30% level at which the first lien test applies. Management has levers: buybacks are discretionary with USD 607 million of authorisation remaining at 2026-10-29, acquisitions can be paused, and capital expenditures are typically below 1.5% of revenue, although about half of employees are covered by collective bargaining agreements, which limits discretion over labour cost. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid distress in a moderate downturn because no scheduled maturity of size falls due before 2029, but the reported covenant headroom is wide and has not been tested independently. facts.label: Downside pathway and outlook
facts.text: Over the next twelve to twenty-four months, tailwinds are regulation-driven inspection demand, infrastructure and technology end markets and the 20.11% earnings growth already shown; headwinds are tariffs, material cost and the integration of three large acquisitions. Management raised full-year guidance for net revenues and adjusted EBITDA in each of the three 2026 releases, to USD 1,235 million to USD 1,255 million of adjusted EBITDA in the latest, but lowered its adjusted free cash flow conversion guidance to 110% from 115% of adjusted net income. ## Findings
### Bottom line

The seven supplied documents support the requested financial, business and credit-synthesis work on APi Group Corp through 30 September 2026, but they do not carry executed debt documents, rating reports or trade quotes, so creditors cannot yet test covenant or instrument terms.

The set holds the 2025 annual report, three 2026 quarterly reports and three earnings releases, the latest dated 29 October 2026, seven days before the as-of date. Legal and covenant text, rating reports, trade quotes and yields, peer financials and fund limits are absent, so those analyses stay blocked or conditional. Guarantor detail and governance rest on partial evidence, because the filings name guarantors only as certain subsidiaries and defer director and ownership detail to a proxy statement that is not supplied.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 60; calculation CALC-1

## Gaps

- The executed credit agreement, its nine amendments and the three senior-note indentures are not supplied. The exhibit lists name them and the filings summarise them, but no operative text is available, so covenant definitions, baskets, call schedules, guarantor release terms and collateral cannot be read. Legal & covenants and Recovery & fulcrum are blocked, and Security selection is conditional on this text. Remedy: obtain the credit agreement through Amendment No. 9 and the indentures for the two 2029 senior notes and the 2034 senior notes.

- No rating agency report is supplied. The only rating statement is in the 2025 lease note, which says the S&P rating of BB and the Moody's corporate family rating of Ba2 were stable in 2025. No issue-level rating, outlook or 2026 rating action is stated, so Ratings & triggers is conditional on an agency report.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 119

- No dated trade quotes, yields or spreads for the notes or the term loan are supplied, and the run settings list no quotes. The only market-based figures are the issuer's own fair value estimates by instrument, which discount cash flows at current rates and are not quotes. Market-implied risk and the pricing side of Security selection cannot be done until a dated quote set is provided.
- No peer financials are supplied. The annual report names a share-return peer group only, and the run settings list no peers, so Peer benchmark is conditional on a peer set.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 58–59
- No portfolio or fund limits are supplied. Committee decision will state the fund's limits as not supplied.

- Governance and ownership evidence is partial. The annual report incorporates director, compensation and ownership detail by reference to a proxy statement that is not supplied; officers and the 2026 officer changes are printed, and no controlling parent or sponsor is named in the supplied text.

- Perimeter is consolidated only. The borrower and note issuer is a wholly owned subsidiary, but the statements are consolidated for the listed registrant, and the supplied text gives no guarantor or non-guarantor summarised information and no list of guarantor subsidiaries. Debt, leverage and cash figures cannot be split by borrower group or guarantor group.

- The issuing entity of the senior notes is described two ways. The liquidity discussion says the wholly owned subsidiary APi Group DE, Inc. completed each offering and the 2034 indenture names it as issuer, while the debt note says the Company completed the 2029 offerings, and the 2025 exhibit index lists the June 2021 indenture as made by APi Group Corporation and the October 2021 indenture as made by APi Escrow Corp., with later supplemental indentures that involve the subsidiary. Both descriptions are kept; the borrower, issuer and guarantor perimeter must be confirmed from the indentures before leverage is read on a borrower-group basis.

- The only maturity ladder is in the annual report and predates the May 2026 amendment and the 2034 notes. The latest quarterly report prints maturity dates but no ladder, and the term loan amortisation is described differently across the reports: the annual report says no quarterly principal is owed, while the latest report states annual instalments of 1.00% of the initial principal, and the initial principal is stated in two ways. Scheduled principal by year therefore cannot be stated from the supplied text. Financial foundation must build the ladder from the debt table and flag this.

- Several 2025 year-end terms are superseded by the Ninth Amendment and must not be carried forward: the term loan maturity moved from 2029 to 2033, the revolver grew from USD 750 million to USD 1,000 million with maturity moving from 2030 to 2031, the covenant exclusion for undrawn letters of credit moved from USD 40 million to USD 60 million, and the first lien net leverage ratio moved from 1.1 times to 1.6 times. The newest report controls each term. These are period changes, not conflicts.

- The release defines a net leverage ratio under the debt agreements, with pro forma adjustments, but prints no value, and the covenant EBITDA definition is in the agreement that is not supplied. Only the first lien ratio is reported, so a covenant-basis total net leverage cannot be shown and headroom to the 3.75 to 1.00 maximum cannot be computed on the agreement definition.

- Cash paid for interest is reported net of interest income, and deferred financing costs are stated in total only, so gross cash interest and carrying value by instrument are not stated. Financial foundation must label the net figure and reconcile principal to carrying value in total.

- The release for the fourth quarter of 2025 is not supplied, so that quarter is derivable only as the year less the first nine months. The full-year guidance update of 2 July 2026 and the current reports of 18 May 2026 are referenced but not supplied.

- The term loan is described as incurred at USD 1,100 million in the annual report and at the then-current balance in the later quarterly reports. The debt table is consistent in every report, so this is a wording difference, and the debt table controls.

spans.text: ## Request

Financial foundation for APi Group Corp (issuer id apg), as of 2026-11-05, on the Full credit assessment pathway. It sets out consolidated annual and interim statements, leverage, interest cover, liquidity and debt for FY2024, FY2025 and the first nine months of 2026, on the registrant's consolidated perimeter in USD millions.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Acquisitions and share repurchases lifted leverage in 2026: total debt reached 3.58x trailing reported EBITDA and net debt 3.21x at 2026-09-30, against 3.13x and 2.10x at the 2025 year end, while liquidity fell to USD 1,032 million.

Cash interest cover rose to 7.74x as earnings grew and cash interest paid fell, but interest expense in the third quarter of 2026 was USD 45 million against USD 34 million a year earlier. The USD 100 million drawn on the revolver after quarter end is not reflected in net debt, and its effect on net debt is not established. Trailing EBITDA carries acquired businesses only from their closing dates and the filings state no pro forma earnings, so run-rate leverage is not established.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation CALC-3; calculation CALC-6; calculation CALC-15
### Key findings

Net debt rose from USD 1,847 million to USD 3,201 million between 2025-12-31 and 2026-09-30, an increase of USD 1,354 million. Acquisitions of USD 1,356 million and share repurchases of USD 252 million over nine months exceeded free cash flow of USD 317 million, and the gap was funded by the 2034 senior notes, revolver borrowing and cash on hand. Added debt raises leverage unless acquired earnings arrive quickly, and the filings state no pro forma earnings for the three large acquisitions.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; calculation CALC-6; calculation CALC-11; calculation CALC-12

Cash flow quality weakened even as earnings grew. Operating cash flow was USD 393 million against USD 377 million a year earlier, but the working capital outflow widened to USD 312 million from USD 218 million, and free cash flow equalled 35.38% of adjusted EBITDA against 41.15%. Working capital absorbed cash because receivables and contract assets grew with revenue, so cash conversion depends on collections keeping pace with growth.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_apg-20260930xexx991.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-11; calculation CALC-16

Liquidity fell by USD 625 million to USD 1,032 million, made up of cash of USD 373 million and undrawn revolver capacity of USD 659 million after USD 6 million of letters of credit. The revolver is drawn USD 335 million, and a further USD 100 million was drawn after quarter end, so availability is USD 559 million at 2026-10-29. Apart from USD 5 million of short-term loans and scheduled term loan amortization, nothing matures before 2029, which limits near-term refinancing pressure, but the 2031 revolver is the only committed facility.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 56; calculation CALC-13; calculation CALC-14

The adjusted figures rest on large add-backs. Systems and business enablement costs of USD 82 million equal 9.15% of nine-month adjusted EBITDA and were USD 61 million a year earlier, so a cost the issuer calls non-recurring has been recurring across periods. Reported EBITDA is therefore the primary denominator, and the adjusted ratios of 3.00x total and 2.69x net are shown beside it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 54–55; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_apg-20260930xexx991.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation CALC-17
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest contrary evidence is earnings momentum: nine-month adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 896 million from USD 746 million, nine-month operating cash flow rose, and the nearest large maturity is the 2029 notes. Adjusted leverage of 3.00x total and 2.69x net at 2026-09-30 is below reported leverage and would fall further if earnings from acquisitions closed during the year were annualised, but the filings do not state those earnings. A partial revolver repayment from operating cash flow, or disclosed pro forma earnings for the acquisitions, would move the view toward lower leverage; further debt-funded acquisitions or a larger working capital outflow would move it the other way.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23; calculation CALC-4
### Limitations

The fiscal-year EBITDA figures are calculated from statement lines because the annual report states only adjusted EBITDA. Cash interest is reported net of interest income, and carrying value is stated only in total, not by instrument. The most recent maturity ladder in the filings predates the 2026 amendment, so the ladder shown is built from instrument maturity dates and puts scheduled term loan amortisation at final maturity. The term loan's security and ranking are not stated, so it is left out of the debt stack.

- Severity high. Covenant headroom cannot be measured: the credit agreement and its EBITDA definition are not supplied, the releases define a net leverage ratio but print no value, and only the first lien ratio is reported. The action is to obtain the credit agreement and compliance certificates.

- Severity high. The term loan's security and ranking, and the guarantor perimeter, are not stated in any supplied document, so the debt stack leaves out the largest facility and borrower-group leverage cannot be shown. The action is to obtain the credit agreement and the indentures.

- Severity medium. No maturity ladder is printed after the 2026 amendment and the 2034 notes, and the term loan amortization base is described two ways, so scheduled principal by year is not established and the ladder shown puts amortization at final maturity. The action is to obtain the amended credit agreement schedule.

- Severity medium. EBITDA for FY2024 and FY2025 is calculated because the annual report states no EBITDA subtotal, and trailing EBITDA at each 2026 date carries acquired businesses only from their closing dates, so run-rate leverage is not established. The action is to obtain pro forma acquired EBITDA for the three large acquisitions.

- Severity medium. Cash interest is reported net of interest income and lags interest expense after the 2034 notes, so gross interest paid is not stated and interest cover on a cash basis is flattered. The action is to obtain gross interest paid and the 2034 coupon dates.

- Severity low. Carrying value by instrument is not disclosed, only the total of deferred financing costs, so each instrument is shown at principal with one financing cost adjustment. The action is to obtain the debt footnote detail.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23

- Severity low. Several statement lines are printed as dashes, for example investment expense in FY2025 and the first quarter of 2025, and no filing line is read as zero; each is stated as not supplied. The action is to treat a dash as nil only where a later filing confirms it.

- Severity low. Balance sheets at 2025-03-31, 2025-06-30 and 2025-09-30 are not in the supplied documents, so prior-year interim net debt and leverage are not established. The action is to obtain the 2025 quarterly reports.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3

- Severity low. Remaining performance obligations are not stated for the 2024 year end or the 2025 quarter ends, and the backlog figure the second-quarter release cites is not defined, so the operating trend covers four dates. The action is to obtain the 2025 quarterly reports and the backlog definition.

- Severity medium. The effect of the borrowing of USD 100 million after quarter end on net debt is not established because the use of proceeds and the cash balance at 2026-10-29 are not stated. The action is to read the next quarterly report.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24

- Severity low. The Q2 and Q3 discrete income statement columns are not printed here; they are reported in the quarterly reports and the stub columns are used to build trailing figures. The action is to add discrete quarters if the forward model needs them.

spans.text: ## Request

Business & governance for APi Group Corp (issuer id apg), as of 2026-11-05, on the Full credit assessment pathway. It sets out the business, revenue mix, operating model, ownership, governance, capital allocation, issuer history and the 2026 transactions that matter to a creditor, from the seven supplied issuer documents.
## Sources

| EX-99.1_2026-07-30_apg-20260630xexx991.htm.jsonl | Earnings release for the second quarter of 2026 (Exhibit 99.1 to a Form 8-K) | 2026-07-30 | f112ae35c8090bbb1d28641903d8fabef87924332451d391abea2504360e0996 | Management statements on backlog and strategy |

## Findings
### Bottom line

APi Group is a diversified safety and specialty services business whose creditor risk comes from acquisition-led financial policy rather than sponsor control, because no controlling sponsor is named in the supplied filings and cash returned to shareholders is small beside acquisition spending.

Revenue is spread across two segments, many customers and several countries, with no customer above 5% of 2025 revenue, but the recurring share of revenue is not quantified. The Series A preferred holder, an entity controlled by a board co-chair, receives an annual dividend that cost USD 590 million of new shares for 2025; it is settled in shares at the board's election, so creditors face dilution of the equity base rather than a cash claim unless that election changes. Board composition, ownership percentages and the legal capacity to pay distributions are not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 134; 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 135–136; calculation CALC-4
### Key findings

The business is diversified by service line, geography and customer, and its largest dependency is Safety Services. Life Safety was 67.14% of nine-month 2026 net revenues, the United States invoiced 67.66% of them, and no single customer exceeded 5% of 2025 net revenues. About half of employees are covered by collective bargaining agreements, which limits how quickly labour cost can be cut in a downturn even though management describes its cost structure as highly variable. Mandated inspection work gives recurring demand in principle, but the share of revenue that recurs is not quantified, so cash-flow durability rests on management's own description.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation CALC-1; calculation CALC-2

Acquisitions are the dominant driver of change and are paid for in cash at closing. In 2026 the three large acquisitions cost USD 271 million, USD 532 million and USD 394 million, and ten smaller ones cost USD 227 million, so the year's acquisition spending reached USD 1,424 million before any acquired earnings. The filings state no pro forma earnings or purchase multiples, so the leverage effect of these purchases cannot be sized from this module's evidence, and the seller of the largest was funds managed by Blackstone Tactical Opportunities. In May the company issued USD 500 million of 2034 senior notes and enlarged its revolver to help fund the later purchases.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-Q_2026-03-31_apg-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation CALC-3

Ownership is not disclosed in the supplied documents beyond one equity-linked instrument that matters to creditors. The Series A preferred, held through a vehicle controlled by a board co-chair, entitles its holder to an annual dividend equal to 20% of the rise in the share price above its previous high-water mark, applied to a fixed block of shares, which was USD 590 million for 2025 and was settled in new shares in January 2026. The dividend is payable in shares or cash at the board's election and the company states it intends to use shares, so the mechanism is dilution today; a cash election would create a large claim that ranks ahead of common equity, and the 2026 dividend and conversion into common shares fall at the end of 2026. A related entity of a co-chair also receives advisory fees of USD 4 million a year, which is small but is cash paid to a shareholder-linked party.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 134; 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 135–136; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30; calculation CALC-4

Financial policy favours growth over deleveraging while keeping cash distributions limited. No cash dividend is paid on common shares and the credit agreement restricts distributions in some situations, but the company has USD 750 million of buyback authorisation remaining after repurchasing about USD 250 million in the nine months of 2026 and USD 75 million in 2025, and in 2024 it paid USD 600 million to repurchase half of the shares from the converted Series B preferred, partly funded by a USD 300 million incremental term loan. Buybacks alongside debt-funded acquisitions raise leverage, and the legal capacity for further distributions is not established because the credit agreement is not supplied.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 137; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 56–57; calculation CALC-5

The finance function has changed recently and its systems are in transition. The chief executive has led the company since 2004, but the chief financial officer has held the role since March 2025 after serving as interim from December 2024, the principal accounting officer designation moved to the chief financial officer from August 2026, and a series of enterprise system implementations began in 2026 with the review of internal controls under way. This matters because reporting reliability underpins monitoring, and because systems and business enablement costs are being added back to adjusted earnings.

Disclosure supports monitoring of results but not of structure. Segment, geography and revenue-line data are given every quarter, but guarantor information, a list of subsidiary guarantors, covenant certificates and the proxy statement are not in the supplied set, and customer contract terms are not described beyond general statements. Creditors can follow operating performance but cannot confirm which entities stand behind the debt.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 2; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that value going to shareholders has mostly been settled in shares or has been small: no cash dividend on common shares, a Series A dividend settled in shares, advisory fees of only USD 4 million a year, and USD 458 million of equity raised in 2024 to help fund the Elevated acquisition. The company has also used amendments to extend maturities and enlarge the revolver rather than to weaken creditor terms, as far as the supplied summaries show. A move to cash settlement of the Series A dividend, repurchases that exceed free cash flow for a sustained period, or a further large acquisition paid mainly in debt would move the view toward higher governance and financial-policy risk. Disclosure of ownership percentages, pro forma acquired earnings and the credit agreement's distribution limits would reduce the uncertainty in either direction.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 134–137; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation CALC-4
### Limitations

- The proxy statement is not supplied, so board independence, director ownership and ownership percentages are not established, which limits the ownership and governance conclusion to the control features visible in the filings.
- The share of revenue from inspection, service and monitoring is not quantified, which leaves the business-quality conclusion resting on management's description of recurring revenue.
- No pro forma earnings are given for the 2026 acquisitions, which prevents sizing the conclusion that acquisitions drive the change in credit risk.
- No executed debt documents are supplied, which means the legal capacity to make distributions, buy back shares or add debt for acquisitions is not assessed in this module.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

CertaSite, a United States inspection-first fire and life safety provider, closed on 2026-02-02 for consideration of USD 271 million, of which USD 268 million was paid in cash at closing. Onyx-Fire Protection Services, a Canadian provider bought from funds managed by Blackstone Tactical Opportunities under an agreement signed on 2026-04-22 for about C$725 in cash, closed on 2026-06-08; the second-quarter report states consideration of USD 522 million and the third-quarter report USD 532 million, a difference of USD 10 million that is not explained. WTech Fire Group, a European fire sprinkler, suppression and detection provider agreed on 2026-04-17 for about EUR 324 in cash, closed on 2026-07-01 for about USD 394 million in cash. The ten smaller acquisitions cost USD 227 million, of which USD 36 million is accrued consideration.

New debt in the period comprised USD 500 million of 5.750% senior notes due 2034, issued by the borrower subsidiary on 2026-05-14 with the net proceeds used for general corporate purposes including funding the announced acquisitions, and the Ninth Amendment to the credit agreement of the same date, which raised the revolver from USD 750 million to USD 1,000 million, lifted the letter of credit sublimit from USD 250 million to USD 300 million, and extended the revolver to 2031-05-14 and the term loan to 2033-05-14. spans.text: ## Request

Fundamental credit for APi Group Corp (issuer id apg), as of 2026-11-05, on the Full credit assessment pathway. It synthesises the source readiness, financial foundation and business and governance work into one creditor view of the issuer's strengths, weaknesses, downside path and monitoring triggers, using the seven supplied issuer documents.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_apg-20260331.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 31 March 2026 | 2026-04-30 | 4f2797670271476a95f9547a3540ae303edaa5e40f3e3f08829817127f41c878 | Checked against the earlier modules for Q1 figures |

| 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 30 September 2026 | 2026-10-29 | 0f3c88ef7de625d84cef8d9062b4481840371b9e18740b974653c45bd1fc951f | Latest statements, debt, liquidity, covenant test, revenue mix, interest expense |

| EX-99.1_2026-07-30_apg-20260630xexx991.htm.jsonl | Earnings release for the second quarter of 2026 (Exhibit 99.1 to a Form 8-K) | 2026-07-30 | f112ae35c8090bbb1d28641903d8fabef87924332451d391abea2504360e0996 | Checked against the earlier modules for Q2 EBITDA and guidance |

| EX-99.1_2026-10-29_apg-20260930xexx991.htm.jsonl | Earnings release for the third quarter of 2026 (Exhibit 99.1 to a Form 8-K) | 2026-10-29 | f776b9079a3057680b637f70cfc8304a121c49085a5098404f23ccab4852f2c3 | Nine-month adjusted EBITDA, free cash flow and guidance |
| Handoff | Module | sha256 | Use |
| Source readiness | CP-0 | 49c022f66e917ac0e688a4c245bcd14e354dc73558a11a31e04cf3d48185130e | Source gaps and absent ratings, market and legal evidence |
| Financial foundation | CP-1 | 52c786a3edcbc24bde8990a4ed5795d4355007032496242f410c3b1db2f7cd51 | Statements, leverage, cover, liquidity, ladder and definitions |
| Business & governance | CP-1A | 18f06440f229f0979e55d05f6ec4a3186d5c704a27de1e81035aad38bacde04d | Business mix, ownership, behaviour flags and governance level |
## Findings
### Bottom line

APi Group's credit profile is adequate but weakening: strong earnings growth in a diversified, inspection-led business has been matched by debt-funded acquisitions that lifted net leverage to 3.21x and cut liquidity, so creditors bear integration and cash-conversion risk until acquired earnings arrive.

The primary downside path is a squeeze on project margins and working capital while the revolver stays drawn and buybacks continue. Net debt of USD 3,201 million at 2026-09-30 excludes a USD 100 million revolver borrowing and a USD 143 million share repurchase after quarter end, and their effect on net debt is not established. Governance and financial-policy risk is at a medium level, and rating, market and legal-document evidence is absent.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation CALC-1; calculation CALC-3
### Key findings

The strongest support is earnings momentum in a diversified business. Nine-month adjusted EBITDA rose 20.11% to USD 896 million, trailing reported EBITDA reached USD 998 million, no customer exceeded 5% of revenue in 2025, and mandated inspection work gives recurring demand, although the recurring share is not quantified. Growth lowers leverage only if it persists, because the added debt is already on the balance sheet.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation CALC-5

The weakest dimension is leverage after debt-funded acquisitions. Net debt rose by USD 1,354 million to USD 3,201 million in nine months, taking net debt to 3.21x trailing reported EBITDA from 2.10x at the 2025 year end and total debt to 3.58x from 3.13x; on adjusted EBITDA the figures are 3.00x total and 2.69x net. Acquisitions and buybacks totalled USD 1,608 million against free cash flow of USD 317 million, so the gap was borrowed or taken from cash. The USD 100 million borrowed on the revolver and the USD 143 million of shares repurchased after quarter end are not reflected, and their effect on net debt is not established.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation CALC-1; calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-14

Interest cover looks strong but is flattered by timing. Trailing EBITDA covers cash interest 7.74x, yet cash interest paid lags the expense, and third-quarter interest expense of USD 45 million is above its year-earlier USD 34 million. On trailing net interest expense cover is 6.98x, and on the third-quarter run rate it is 5.54x, so cover is likely to fall toward the lower figures as the 2034 notes pay a full year of interest.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation CALC-2; calculation CALC-9

Liquidity is adequate but thinner and more dependent on the revolver. Cash and undrawn revolver fell from USD 1,657 million at 2025 year end to USD 1,032 million, and the revolver is 33.50% drawn against a 30% usage level above which a first lien net leverage test with a maximum of 3.75x applies; the issuer reports 1.6x at quarter end, wide against that maximum, but the covenant definitions are not supplied, so the reported figure cannot be tied to the leverage computed here.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 59–60; calculation CALC-3; calculation CALC-4

Cash conversion has weakened as working capital absorbs growth. Free cash flow was 35.38% of adjusted EBITDA in nine months against 41.15%, the working capital outflow was USD 312 million against USD 218 million, and the gross margin fell to 30.82% from 31.22% on mix and material costs. This is the first place a slowdown in contracting work would show, because customer advances of USD 902 million would unwind if billings slowed.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-10-29_apg-20260930xexx991.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; calculation CALC-6; calculation CALC-7; calculation CALC-9; calculation CALC-11

Refinancing capacity rests on a long-dated maturity profile and a recent successful issue rather than on current ratings. No scheduled maturity of size falls before 2029, when USD 614 million of senior notes mature, and USD 500 million of 2034 notes were placed in May 2026, but the balance sheet classes USD 361 million of debt as current at 2026-09-30 against USD 5 million at the 2025 year end and the filings do not break it down; the only rating statement is a 2025 note giving BB and Ba2 as stable, and no agency report or market price is supplied.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Source readiness (CP-0); 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 119; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23; calculation CALC-8; calculation CALC-14

Financial policy risk is medium. Acquisitions and buybacks raise leverage while cash payouts to shareholders stay modest and the Series A dividend is settled in shares, but a further USD 143 million of shares was repurchased in October while the revolver was drawn a further USD 100 million, and the legal capacity for distributions and acquisitions cannot be tested without the credit agreement.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation CALC-14
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a better view is that trailing figures include acquired businesses only from their closing dates, so leverage of 3.21x net may overstate the run-rate, and that earnings have grown 20.11% in nine months with no maturity pressure until 2029. If acquired earnings are disclosed and are material, or if the revolver is repaid from operating cash flow, leverage could fall toward the year-end level. The strongest evidence for a worse view is that interest cover on current expense is lower than on cash paid, that free cash flow conversion fell, and that the legal limits on further debt-funded buybacks and acquisitions are unknown. A further large debt-funded acquisition, a rise in revolver use, or a margin fall below the current 30.82% would move the view toward weaker credit quality.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-1; calculation CALC-2; calculation CALC-5; calculation CALC-9
### Limitations

- Ratings are stated only for 2025 in a lease note and no agency report or market price is supplied, so the refinancing conclusion rests on the issuer's own funding record rather than on evidence of current market access.

- The springing covenant is known only from its summary, so the liquidity conclusion cannot test the reported headroom independently and treats the 30% usage level as a signal, not a confirmed breach condition.
- Acquired earnings are not annualised in any supplied figure, so the leverage conclusion could be more cautious than run-rate leverage by an amount the filings do not state.
- Board and ownership detail is missing, so the medium governance risk level rests on documented behaviour alone and a higher or lower level cannot be excluded.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Credit strengths are the diversified, inspection-led service model, earnings momentum and a long-dated maturity profile. The service model spreads revenue across two segments, many customers and several countries, and inspection work is often required by law or insurance, which supports demand through a downturn; nine-month adjusted EBITDA growth of 20.11% shows that demand is converting into earnings. Debt matures late, with USD 614 million due in 2029, USD 335 million of revolver in 2031, USD 2,147 million of term loan in 2033 and USD 500 million of notes in 2034, so scheduled refinancing pressure is distant.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-5; calculation CALC-8

Credit weaknesses are rising leverage, thinner liquidity and weaker cash conversion. Net leverage of 3.21x against 2.10x at the year end reflects acquisitions and buybacks funded by debt and cash; liquidity fell by USD 625 million; and free cash flow conversion fell as working capital grew. A related weakness is the lack of evidence on legal capacity and ownership, which leaves the limits on further distributions and borrowing unknown.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-1; calculation CALC-3; calculation CALC-6
### Downside pathway and outlook

The realistic downside starts with slower contracting demand or higher tariff-driven material costs. Growth is concentrated in the lower-margin Specialty Services segment, which is 32.92% of revenue, grew 26.63% in nine months against 13.07% for Safety Services and earns a segment margin of 10.87% against 16.74%, so a slowdown there would be expected to hit earnings and working capital first. Lower volume and margin reduce earnings and leave working capital tied up, so free cash flow weakens while acquisition integration costs and buybacks continue; the revolver then funds the gap, undrawn liquidity falls below its current USD 1,032 million, and revolver use stays above the 30% level at which the first lien test applies. Management has levers: buybacks are discretionary with USD 607 million of authorisation remaining at 2026-10-29, acquisitions can be paused, and capital expenditures are typically below 1.5% of revenue, although about half of employees are covered by collective bargaining agreements, which limits discretion over labour cost. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid distress in a moderate downturn because no scheduled maturity of size falls due before 2029, but the reported covenant headroom is wide and has not been tested independently.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 59–60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation CALC-4; calculation CALC-12; calculation CALC-14

Over the next twelve to twenty-four months, tailwinds are regulation-driven inspection demand, infrastructure and technology end markets and the 20.11% earnings growth already shown; headwinds are tariffs, material cost and the integration of three large acquisitions. Management raised full-year guidance for net revenues and adjusted EBITDA in each of the three 2026 releases, to USD 1,235 million to USD 1,255 million of adjusted EBITDA in the latest, but lowered its adjusted free cash flow conversion guidance to 110% from 115% of adjusted net income. The guidance supports the near-term earnings view and is management outlook, not evidence, and the lower conversion guidance fits the weaker cash conversion shown above.
